Gene prediction and annotation of the most complete bins with Prokka. Commands for this step were run in `prokka/`.

# Step 7. Find and annotate genes with prokka

The ultimate goal is to use the BBD metagenome to improve our understanding of metabolic processes within the mat. To do this we first need to find the genes in each bin and, where possible, assign them a name and function based on homologous genes of known function.

Moved into the `prokka` folder

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
```

Looked at the list of top bins from step 5 to pick one to test with

```{bash}
cat ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Tested Prokka on a single bin first, `metabat.66`

```{bash}
bin=metabat.66
prokka --cpus 2 --outdir $bin --prefix $bin  ../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa
```

Listed the output folder. It worked, and the `.tsv` file with each gene's name and functional information was there

```{bash}
ls metabat.66
```

Then ran Prokka on all the top bins. This is computationally intensive, so I used a slurm script, [run_prokka.sh](prokka/run_prokka.sh), saved in `prokka`

The script loops over the bins in `bbd_topbins.txt` and annotates each one


Submitted the job (job 498). It ran overnight
The gtdbtk job (job 495) was running at the time and was also done the next day.

```{bash}
sbatch run_prokka.sh
```
